**Service Name:** MindWell Sleep Study

This study is about a sleep-tracking app and its effects on people with insomnia. Here are the key points:

* **Purpose:** The study wants to see how a sleep-tracking app affects people with insomnia.
* **What's required:** Participants wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete a weekly survey. This is the only thing you have to do.
* **Risks:** There's a small risk of skin irritation from the sensor strap.
* **Data sharing:** Your data won't be shared publicly, but de-identified data (data without your name or personal info) might be sent to universities helping the study. Your personal data will only be seen by the researchers.
* **Withdrawal:** You can leave the study at any time and it won't affect you.
* **Compensation:** When you finish the study, you'll receive $75.

Be aware of the following things that might affect you: 
* As with any study involving sensitive data, there's a concern about data protection.
* It might be a bit annoying to wear a wrist sensor, and there's the risk of skin irritation.
* If you decide not to participate, you won't get any compensation.

If you have questions, you can contact the IRB, a research review group, at irb@example.edu.
source_tos:
INFORMED CONSENT — MINDWELL SLEEP STUDY

1. PURPOSE. This study examines the effects of a sleep-tracking app on insomnia.
2. PROCEDURES. Participants wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete weekly surveys.
3. RISKS. Minimal risk: skin irritation from the sensor strap.
4. DATA. De-identified data may be shared with collaborating universities. Identifiable data will not be shared outside the research team.
5. WITHDRAWAL. You may withdraw at any time without penalty.
6. COMPENSATION. Participants receive $75 upon completion.
7. CONTACT. For questions contact the IRB at irb@example.edu.

**Service Name:** Google Terms of Service (Effective 2024)

The Google Terms of Service outline the rules and guidelines for using Google's products and services. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to Google's various products and services listed on the company's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content to Google, it can be used to improve and train the company's AI and machine learning systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Google's Privacy Policy explains how the company collects and processes personal data. You can find more information in the Privacy Policy.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration, which means you and Google will use a private process instead of going to court. However, there's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the live document.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Generative AI features**: The terms prohibit abusing and reverse-engineering AI models, which might be restrictive for some users. (Generative AI features are used to improve Google's AI services, like those used in search results or language translation.)
* **Binding arbitration**: This means you'll use a private dispute process instead of taking Google to court. While there's a 30-day opt-out window, this clause might be a concern if you prefer to have the option to go to court.

**Red Flags:**

* None specifically. These terms seem to follow the standard practice of requiring users to agree to the terms as a condition of using Google's services.

**Where to Find More Information:**

* Google's Privacy Policy, which explains how the company collects and processes personal data.
* The live Google Terms of Service document and the previous version for comparison (available at [https://policies.google.com/terms](https://policies.google.com/terms?hl=en-US)).
* Google's published legal contact information for questions or concerns about these terms (listed at [https://policies.google.com/terms](https://policies.google.com/terms?hl=en-US)).

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GOOGLE TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Google and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: Added language about generative AI features (e.g. content used to improve Google's AI services), clarified that abuse and reverse-engineering of AI models are prohibited, and updated the disputes/arbitration and liability sections. Comparison page provided by Google: policies.google.com/terms/archive/20220105-20240522.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Google to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policies.google.com/terms?hl=en-US . The previous version is available at https://policies.google.com/terms/archive/20220105?hl=en-US .

**Service Name:** Microsoft Services Agreement

**Summary:** These terms govern your usage of Microsoft products and services, such as Xbox, and apply to the services listed on Microsoft's official terms page. The agreement governs your rights, data, and responsibilities when using these services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Your Content:** Microsoft can use the data and content you submit to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The terms rely on Microsoft's published Privacy Policy, which outlines what personal data is collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If a dispute arises, most services require binding arbitration with a class-action waiver. This means you'll resolve disputes privately, rather than in court, and you won't be able to join a class-action lawsuit.
* **Termination:** Either Microsoft or you can terminate the agreement under the conditions specified in this document.

**Potential issues:**

* **Data usage:** Microsoft can use your personal data to train their AI/ML systems (see **Your Content**, section 4). While this is not directly stated as an exploitative practice, it might raise concerns about data protection.
* **Dispute resolution:** Mandatory binding arbitration with class-action waivers (see **Dispute Resolution**, section 5) can make it difficult for users to seek redress or join a class-action lawsuit.

Remember to review Microsoft's published Privacy Policy and the linked Updates page to understand how your data is used and protected.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Added a new 'exportable data' subsection under Your Content, clarified that some services may have separate support terms, added language that some trial offers may require auto-renewal, and updated Xbox service-specific terms regarding sign-in to non-Microsoft platforms. Documented in Microsoft's Updates page (servicesagreement/Updates).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ . The previous version is available at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/upcoming.aspx .

response:
The Terms of Service (TOS) is for the Microsoft Services Agreement, which applies to various products and services offered by Microsoft.

Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

* **Scope**: These terms outline the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services listed on Microsoft's official terms page.
* **What's changed**: The 2024 version adds clarifications on moderation and user data tracking on Xbox and third-party platforms.
* **Content and licensing**: Microsoft uses user-submitted content to improve and train its AI systems, but this is subject to the user's settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: Microsoft's Privacy Policy sets out how it collects and processes personal data.
* **Dispute resolution**: Users may need to participate in binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. However, users with new accounts have a 30-day window to opt out.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to specific conditions in the live document.

Some potentially concerning clauses for users include:

**Service Name:** OpenAI Terms of Use (Consumer)

These Terms of Service are the rules that govern your relationship with OpenAI, the company that provides various products and services through their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These Terms of Service apply to the products and services listed on OpenAI's official terms page. If you're using OpenAI's services, these rules apply to you.
* **Content and License**: OpenAI uses the content you submit to improve their AI and machine learning systems, but only to the extent you allow and in accordance with the law.
* **Privacy**: The company has a separate **Privacy Policy** that explains how they collect and process your personal data. Make sure to read it to understand how your data is used.
* **Dispute Resolution**: In case of a dispute, you're required to go through **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you can't file a class-action lawsuit against OpenAI.
* **Termination**: Either you or OpenAI can end the agreement under the conditions described in the live document.
* **Contact**: If you have questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information.

**Potential issues:**

* **Dispute Resolution**: The requirement of binding arbitration with a class-action waiver might make it difficult for users to pursue large-scale claims against OpenAI.
* **Termination**: The terms of termination are not detailed in this summary, and users should review the live document for specific conditions.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI TERMS OF USE (CONSUMER) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Split the consumer Terms of Use from a separate Business Terms (for API/Enterprise) effective January 31, 2024, switched arbitration provider from ADR Services to National Arbitration and Mediation, and revised the dispute-resolution and batch-arbitration procedures. Documented at help.openai.com/en/articles/8541945.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use .

**Service Name:** OpenAI Services Agreement (Business/API)

**Summary:** 

These Terms of Service outline the rules and responsibilities between you (the user) and OpenAI for using their business and API services. They essentially cover how you can use OpenAI's products, what happens to the data you provide, and what to expect in case of disputes.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to your relationship with OpenAI and all the services they offer, as listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you provide content to OpenAI, they use it to run, improve, and train their AI systems. The usage is subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** OpenAI has a separate Privacy Policy that explains what personal data they collect and how it's processed. The Terms of Service point to this document for more information.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You're required to use binding arbitration to resolve disputes, which means giving up the right to take the case to court. This also means you can't join a class-action lawsuit against OpenAI. However, you have a 30-day window to opt out of this arbitration requirement for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement as described in the live document. The current terms don't detail the conditions for termination.

**Potential Harm to Users:**

* **Class-action lawsuit waiver:** Users can't join a class-action lawsuit against OpenAI if there's a dispute. This means you might need to resolve issues individually, which can be time-consuming and might limit your ability to seek collective redress.
* **Arbitration requirement:** Users are required to use binding arbitration, which may limit their ability to seek relief through the courts.

The Terms of Service do not address the following topics:
* How often OpenAI updates its services or the Terms of Service
* What specific types of data OpenAI collects
* The specific process for termination or how it applies to users

Please note that while I've tried to provide a summary and highlight potential issues, these Terms of Service are written in a way that might be difficult to navigate for non-experts. It's always a good idea to review the actual document and seek advice from a qualified professional if you're unsure about anything.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI SERVICES AGREEMENT (BUSINESS/API) (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Replaced the prior Business Terms with a single OpenAI Services Agreement effective May 31, 2025, covering API, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Team and other business services, with updated provisions on data handling, indemnification and SLAs. Announcement: community.openai.com/t/new-openai-services-agreement-effective-may-31-2025/1249405.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://openai.com/policies/business-terms/ .

These are the Anthropic Consumer Terms of Service terms that govern the user's relationship with Anthropic.

**Key Provisions:**

### 1. **Scope**
These terms specifically apply to products and services outlined on Anthropic's official terms page. That means if Anthropic offers other products or services not listed, these terms might not apply to those.

### 2. **User Content**
Anthropic uses contents uploaded by users to improve its AI/ML systems, as long as this aligns with the user's settings and applicable laws. (In other words, users own their content, but Anthropic has rights to use it for specific purposes.)

### 3. **Privacy**
Private data collected by Anthropic is governed by its published Privacy Policy, not these Terms of Service.

### 4. **Dispute Resolution**
In case of a problem, Anthropic requires binding arbitration with class-action waivers, which means that individuals may not join a class-action lawsuit against the company. However, users can opt out within 30 days of creating their account.

### 5. **Termination**
Either the user or Anthropic can end the agreement by following the terms described in the document.

### 6. **Contact**
For questions about these terms, contact Anthropic through their published contact information.

**Potential Concerns:**
* **Limiting class-action lawsuits:** This means that individual users may not join group lawsuits against Anthropic, which might limit their ability to hold the company accountable for large-scale issues. However, users can opt out within 30 days.
* **Arbitration (private dispute process) instead of traditional court proceedings**

Note: The Terms of Service seem more transparent overall, but users should review all terms carefully, especially the Acceptable Use Policy and sections on business and enterprise usage.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Updated effective October 8, 2025: clarified scope (Claude.ai, Claude Pro, Claude apps), added explicit Acceptable Use Policy reference, refined provisions on business/enterprise email-domain linking, and updated dispute-resolution and governing-law sections. Versioning tracked at tostracker.app/document/anthropic.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms .

**Service Name:** Anthropic Commercial Terms of Service (API)

These terms apply to businesses or organizations using Anthropic's products and services, particularly their commercial API offerings.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** The terms cover the relationship between the user and Anthropic and apply to the company's commercial products and services.
* **Content and License:** When customers submit content, Anthropic uses it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The terms reference Anthropic's published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process customer data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes are resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. However, there's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the live document.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Customer Data Use:** While Anthropic uses customer content as agreed, the text is not explicit about how they'll use it for training (except by default).
* **Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers:** This provision might make it harder for customers to join class-action lawsuits or seek public accountability.

Some questions customers might want to ask Anthropic include:

* How is customer data specifically used for training, and are there any restrictions on the types of prompts or completions that trigger model training?
* Are there any alternatives to binding arbitration, given the potential limitations of this dispute resolution method?

**Contact Information:**

For questions about these terms, check the company's published legal contact information at: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC COMMERCIAL TERMS OF SERVICE (API) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added more detailed sections on customer data and outputs, clarified that customer prompts and completions are not used to train models by default, and updated indemnification and acceptable-use language tied to the published Usage Policy.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms .

**Service Name:** Meta (previously Facebook) Terms of Service

**Summary:** These Terms of Service outline the relationship between you (the user) and Meta, the company behind the services you're using. This document explains how your user-submitted content will be used, how to resolve disputes, and other important rules governing your use of Meta's products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms apply to the products and services listed on Meta's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Meta's services, you grant them permission to use it for their operations, improvements, and to train their AI systems. This is subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** The Terms reference Meta's separate Privacy Policy, which outlines what data is collected and how it's used. (Note: The Privacy Policy is not included in these Terms, and you should check it separately.)
* **Dispute Resolution:** Both you and Meta agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but check the live document for details.
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement under certain conditions.
* **Contact:** For questions about these Terms, check Meta's published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses:** The following provisions may affect your rights:

* **Dispute Resolution:** Requiring binding arbitration with class-action waivers may limit your ability to join class-action lawsuits and could lead to higher costs for resolving disputes.
* **Termination:** Meta can end the agreement under certain conditions, which may limit your access to their services.

Please note that these Terms are subject to change, and you should regularly review the live document to stay informed about any updates.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FACEBOOK / META TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Facebook) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 1, 2025: tightened opening agreement language ('using these products means you agree'), added clearer license framing for content uploaded to Meta Products, and added wording about Meta's use of AI/machine-learning systems on user content for service improvement and safety.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Facebook) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.facebook.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.facebook.com/terms .

The service being described is called the "Instagram Terms of Use."

Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms govern your relationship with Meta (the company that owns Instagram) and apply to all Instagram products and services.
* **Content and License**: When you upload content to Instagram, you give Meta a non-exclusive, worldwide license to use, distribute, and modify your content. This means Instagram can use your photos and videos to improve its services and even train its AI systems, as long as you have allowed it to do so under your account settings.
* **Privacy**: Instagram's Privacy Policy explains how your personal data is collected and processed. These terms simply reference this policy, so you'll need to read the Privacy Policy to understand how your data is handled.
* **Dispute Resolution**: If you have a dispute with Instagram, you'll need to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court). You have 30 days from creating an account to opt out of this requirement, but after that, you won't be able to use class-action lawsuits.
* **Termination**: Either you or Instagram can terminate the agreement at any time, subject to certain conditions that are detailed in the live document.

**Provisions that May be Harmful to the User:**

* **Binding Arbitration**: Requiring binding arbitration with class-action waivers can limit your ability to sue Instagram in court. This can make it harder for you to seek compensation or change Instagram's policies.
* **Global License**: Granting a non-exclusive, worldwide license to use your content can limit your control over how your content is used. While this license is non-exclusive, it still gives Instagram significant rights to your content.

**Additional Information:**

* If you have any questions about these terms, you can contact Instagram through the help center at https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870.
* The previous version of these terms is available in an archived form at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870.

Please note that this summary is based on the current Terms of Service and may not reflect any changes or updates that may occur in the future.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — INSTAGRAM TERMS OF USE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Instagram) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Aligned with the Meta umbrella update effective January 1, 2025: explicit grant of a worldwide non-exclusive license to use, distribute and modify uploaded content, and new wording referencing AI features and data processing across Meta Products.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Instagram) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 .

Keep in mind that these terms are subject to change, and it's essential to review the document periodically to ensure you're comfortable with any updates.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — X TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with X (Twitter) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective November 15, 2024: added an explicit, royalty-free, worldwide license for X to use posted content for training machine-learning and generative-AI models, removed the prior in-product opt-out language, and broadened third-party data-sharing permissions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by X (Twitter) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://x.com/en/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240515000000*/https://twitter.com/en/tos .

response:
**TikTok Terms of Service (US)**

These are the terms that govern your use of TikTok in the United States.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to TikTok's products and services, as listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content to TikTok, you grant the company a license to use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems.
* **Privacy**: TikTok collects personal data from users, and their Privacy Policy explains how this data is processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: If you have a dispute with TikTok, you'll participate in binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court), with some exceptions.
* **Termination**: Either you or TikTok can terminate the agreement, subject to certain conditions.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Generative-AI Rules**: TikTok is explicit that their AI output should be accepted as-is, and that users are responsible for both input and output. This means that users may inadvertently create or share content generated by AI.
* **Automatic License**: By using TikTok, you're giving them a sublicense to use your content for training their AI/ML models. While this is likely a common practice, it may be troubling for users who value their creative work.
* **Arbitration**: The terms require binding arbitration, which prevents users from joining a class-action lawsuit. This might limit an individual's ability to hold TikTok accountable for widespread problems.
* **Term Unclear**: The terms state that either party can terminate the agreement, but the specific conditions for termination are not clearly outlined.

**Important Considerations:**

* Before using TikTok, make sure you understand how your content will be used and shared.
* Take notice of the Privacy Policy and how personal data is processed.
* Be aware of the generative-AI rules to avoid inadvertently sharing AI-generated content.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TIKTOK TERMS OF SERVICE (US) (Effective 2026; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with TikTok and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective January 22, 2026: contracting party changed to TikTok USDS following the US joint venture; added explicit generative-AI rules (output 'as is', user responsibility for inputs/outputs, prohibition on stripping watermarks or claiming AI output is human-made); reaffirmed sublicensable license to use content for training ML models.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by TikTok to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en .

**Scope:** The terms govern your relationship with Adobe when you use their products and services listed on their official terms page.

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ADOBE GENERAL TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Adobe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: February 2024 update added language allowing Adobe to access user content via 'automated and manual methods' to improve services and software. After backlash in June 2024, Adobe rewrote sections in clearer language, explicitly stating it does not train generative-AI models on customer cloud content and added a plain-English summary of changes.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Adobe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html .

The service referred to here is the "LinkedIn User Agreement."

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** The Terms of Service (or TOS) govern your relationship with LinkedIn, which includes the company's products and services. The TOS apply to all users, worldwide.
* **Content and License:** When you provide content on LinkedIn, you grant the company permission to use it to operate and improve its services. This includes using the content to train artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems. You can opt out of this use by changing your settings.
* **Privacy Policy:** The TOS cross-reference LinkedIn's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data the company collects and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The TOS require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court) for disputes. This means that you'll have to resolve disputes with LinkedIn outside of a public court. Additionally, class-action lawsuits are waived. However, for new accounts, you have a 30-day opt-out window to prevent arbitration.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions listed in the live document.

**Concerns for Users:**

* The class-action waiver and binding arbitration provisions may be challenging for users, as they limit access to the court system and the ability to pursue group claims against LinkedIn.
* The use of user-submitted content to train AI and ML systems may raise concerns about data protection and ownership. However, users have an opt-out toggle to control this use, if desired.
* The dispute resolution provisions emphasize private arbitration over public court proceedings, which may not be favorable for users seeking greater transparency and accountability.

Please note that this is a general summary of the key provisions, and you should carefully review the full Terms of Service for a detailed understanding of your rights and responsibilities as a LinkedIn user.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — LINKEDIN USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with LinkedIn and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: November 20, 2024 update added explicit references to use of member data and content to train generative AI models for LinkedIn features (with an opt-out toggle in Settings). Also updated dispute-resolution and class-action waiver provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by LinkedIn to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement . The previous version is available at https://www.linkedin.com/legal/previous-user-agreement .

**Service Name:** Slack User Terms of Service

The Slack User Terms of Service govern your relationship with Slack, the company behind the popular communication platform. Below is a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope:** These terms apply to Slack products and services, as listed on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Slack, they can use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems (think chatbots and predictive features). However, they'll follow your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Slack references their published Privacy Policy, which details what data they collect and how it's processed. It's essential to review their Privacy Policy for a clear understanding of data practices.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The term requires binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means you'll need to opt-out of arbitration within 30 days of creating your account if you want to pursue a class-action lawsuit.
* **Termination:** Either Slack or you can terminate the agreement based on the conditions outlined in the live document.
* **Contact:** For questions about the terms, visit Slack's published legal contact information.

**Clauses That May be Harmful to the User:**

* **Binding Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers:** This provision may limit your ability to join a class-action lawsuit against Slack. It's essential to understand this clause and opt-out within 30 days if you prefer the option to join a class-action lawsuit.

**Important Note:** If you're unsure about any clause, it's always a good idea to review the document and consult with a legal expert.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SLACK USER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Slack and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Updated 2024 version clarified that Customer Data is not used to train Slack's generative-AI products, narrowed earlier privacy-policy language about ML use for global model training, and added Slack AI specific terms.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Slack to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://slack.com/terms-of-service/user . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000*/https://slack.com/terms-of-service/user .

[EXPECTED SUMMARY POINTS]

The Terms of Service govern the relationship between you and GitHub, a software development platform. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**What the Terms cover:** These Terms apply to GitHub's products and services, as described on their official terms page.

**How your content is used:** When you contribute content to GitHub, it may be used to improve their services, train their AI systems, and operate the platform. However, your preferences around using this data will be respected.

**Data sharing:** GitHub can share your personal data with their affiliates, such as Microsoft, for the purpose of developing AI and machine learning models. Your data can also be used to train AI features. You can opt out of this data sharing with your account settings.

**Dispute resolution:** If you have a dispute with GitHub, you and the company will use binding arbitration, which is a private dispute process instead of going to court. You can opt out of this process within 30 days of creating your account if you don't agree.

**Termination:** Either you or GitHub can terminate the agreement at any time, subject to certain conditions.

**Key provisions to note:**

* **Data sharing:** GitHub can share your personal data with their affiliates for AI/ML development and AI feature training.
* **Binding arbitration:** If you have a dispute with GitHub, you will use a private dispute process instead of going to court, with limited opportunity to opt out.
* **Opt-out window:** You have a 30-day opt-out window when creating your account to refuse binding arbitration.

These Terms of Service do not address your rights or remedies outside of the binding arbitration process if you're not satisfied with the outcome of the dispute resolution process.

Please note that these Terms may change over time, and you should check the updated version for any changes.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GITHUB TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2026; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with GitHub and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: March 2026 update expanded the Affiliates section so personal data may be shared with Microsoft and other GitHub affiliates for AI/ML model development, added a new product-development purpose for using personal data to train AI features, and clarified that user opt-out preferences propagate to affiliates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by GitHub to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NETFLIX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected the household sharing/'extra member' policy: paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members, added clearer language on what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', and updated billing/cancellation provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Netflix to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse .

**PayPal User Agreement**

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services offered on the company's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These Terms apply to all users and encompass various products and services offered by PayPal.
* **Content and License**: PayPal may use user-submitted content to improve and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: The Terms reference PayPal's published Privacy Policy, which describes the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most cases require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but Steam is an exception.
* **Termination**: Either party may terminate the agreement according to the conditions described in the document.
* **Contact**: For questions, see PayPal's published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* The requirement for **binding arbitration with class-action waivers** may limit your ability to join a class-action lawsuit against PayPal. This can make it more difficult for affected users to seek collective compensation for unfair practices.
* The **30-day opt-out window for new accounts** may not be sufficient for users to make an informed decision about binding arbitration.
* **Termination** can be initiated by either party, which may result in the loss of access to PayPal services and funds.

Please note that these Terms of Service aim to provide a summary of the key provisions. If you have specific questions or concerns, it's essential to review the full document.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

**Service Name:**
Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions (2024)

**Key Provisions:**

* These terms govern your relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services listed on Apple's official terms page.
* Apple uses your submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* Apple's Privacy Policy sets out the personal data collected and how it's processed.
* Binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) is required to resolve disputes, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

**Flagged Clauses:**
* **Binding Arbitration with Class-Action Waiver**: This means that if you have a dispute with Apple, you'll have to resolve it through private arbitration instead of going to court. Additionally, you'll give up your right to participate in a class-action lawsuit. This clause may be harmful to users as it can limit their ability to seek compensation in cases where many users are affected.

Other important notes:
* Apple can terminate the agreement with or without cause, subject to conditions described in the live document.
* Your submitted content is subject to the terms, and Apple may use it to improve its services.

It's essential to understand that these terms are in place to protect Apple's interests and may not necessarily prioritize your rights as a user. However, these terms are standard in the tech industry, and it's crucial to familiarize yourself with them to know what you're getting into.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

**Service Name: iCloud Terms and Conditions**

**Summary of Key Provisions:**

These Terms of Service, effective as of 2024, govern your relationship with Apple when using Apple's iCloud services. Here's a summary of key provisions:

* **Scope**: These terms apply to Apple's products and services listed on their official terms page.
* **Content**: Apple uses user-submitted content to operate and improve its services, including training AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: The terms reference Apple's published Privacy Policy, which sets out how personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most users must agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement subject to conditions described in the live document.

**Harmful Clauses:**

1. **Mandatory Arbitration and Class-Action Waivers**: You may be required to use private arbitration instead of going to court, and you may be blocked from joining a class-action lawsuit together with other users who have similar complaints.
2. **Loss of Control Over Personal Data**: Apple uses user-submitted content to improve its services, which may include AI/ML training, without explicit user consent.
3. **Termination Without Reason**: Either party can terminate the agreement subject to conditions not disclosed here. This means Apple can suspend or terminate your account without notice or explanation.

To understand more about Apple's data handling practices, you should also review their [published Privacy Policy](https://www.apple.com/privacy/).
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

**Service Name**: The Terms of Service for the Snapchat service, owned by Snap.

**Plain-Language Summary**:

These Terms of Service outline the agreement between you (the user) and Snap (the owner of Snapchat). The key provisions are:

* **What the agreement covers**: These Terms apply to Snapchat and its related services.
* **How your content is used**: You grant Snap the right to use, operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems with your submitted content (unless you've opted out).
* **Data sharing**: Snap collects personal data from you and shares it with you as a parent via the Family Center, if you're under 18.
* **Disputes**: You and Snap agree to binding arbitration, which means you'll use a private process instead of going to court to resolve disputes (you have a 30-day window to opt out).
* **Termination**: Either party can cancel this agreement under certain conditions.
* **Contact**: If you have questions, refer to Snap's published contact information.

**Potential Issues**: Some clauses may be problematic for users:

* **Arbitration** (clause 5): This binding arbitration may be unfair to users, as they give up the right to go to court. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Limited control over content**: These Terms suggest that Snap may use your content without requiring explicit permission (clause 3).
* **Data sharing**: As a parent or under-18 user, your data is shared with Family Center (clause 2 is unclear without additional context).
* **Limited termination options**: While either party can cancel the agreement, the conditions for doing so are not clearly outlined (clause 7).

Keep in mind that these potential issues don't necessarily imply Snap's website or service is malicious; rather, they highlight aspects of the agreement that may be unfavorable to users.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SNAP TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Snap (Snapchat) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective April 7, 2025: added new sections on My AI and other generative-AI features, expanded the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, clarified data-sharing with parents (for under-18 users via Family Center), and updated arbitration pre-dispute notice procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.snap.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.snap.com/terms .

response:
Here's a summary of the Terms of Service:

**Service Name:** Tumblr's Terms of Service govern how you use the Tumblr service, which includes its products and services as described on the official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* The terms apply to your relationship with Tumblr, which means they cover what Tumblr promises to do (or not do) for you, and what you agree to do (or not do) when using the service.
* The main change in the latest update involves how Tumblr uses your public content for artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) training, based on a deal with their AI partners. Here are the key points related to this change:

**Service Name:** Notion Terms of Service.

**Key Provisions:**

* These terms explain your relationship with Notion and cover its products and services.
* Content you submit is used by Notion to operate, improve its services, and train its AI/ML systems (subject to your settings and applicable law).
* Notion's Privacy Policy is cross-referenced for more information on the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* Disputes will mostly be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court) with some exceptions. You have 30 days to opt-out of this arrangement if you create a new account.
* Either party can end the agreement under certain conditions, which are detailed in the live document.

**Clauses that may be potentially harmful to the user:**

* **Content and License:** This provision states that content submitted by the user can be used by Notion for various purposes, including training its AI/ML systems. This could potentially infringe upon a user's copyright or intellectual property rights.
* **DISPUTE RESOLUTION:** The use of binding arbitration might not be favorable for users who prefer to take their disputes to court. This process might also make it harder to join class-action lawsuits.
* **TERMINATION:** Users should carefully review the conditions for terminating the agreement, as it might be challenging to do so in certain situations.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NOTION TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Notion and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Notion AI provisions (input/output ownership, no training of foundational models on customer data by default), updated subprocessor list, and clarified data-residency options for enterprise plans.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Notion to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.notion.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.notion.so/terms .

**Service Name:** Stack Overflow Public Network Terms of Service (2024 version)

The Terms of Service are agreements between you and Stack Overflow that govern your relationship with the company and its services. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all products and services described on Stack Overflow's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Stack Overflow, the company uses it to operate, improve, and sometimes train its AI and machine learning systems. The license allows for non-commercial use, but commercial use may require a separate agreement.
* **Privacy:** The terms refer to Stack Overflow's separate Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. You can find the Privacy Policy elsewhere on the website.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If there's a conflict, Stack Overflow requires binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with certain restrictions (class-action waivers, but with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts). Note that not all cases are subject to this requirement.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions specified in the document.
* **Contact:** To ask questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information on the website.

As for potentially **harmful clauses for the user:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** The binding arbitration requirement may limit your access to court and potentially make it harder to join a class-action lawsuit.
* **Generative AI / LLM Restriction:** Although this clause explicitly licenses user-submitted content under CC BY-SA, it restricts bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, which might limit how users can reuse their own content for non-commercial purposes.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STACK OVERFLOW PUBLIC NETWORK TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: May 2024 update added a 'Generative AI / LLM' restriction explicitly licensing posted Q&A under CC BY-SA but limiting bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, after the company's content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stack Overflow to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public .

The Terms of Service are for Quora, a platform for users to ask and answer questions.

Here's a summary of the key provisions:

* **Relationship with Quora**: These Terms govern your relationship with Quora and apply to the various products and services offered by the company, as detailed on Quora's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Quora uses your user-submitted content (e.g., answers, comments) to operate, improve, and train its AI and Machine Learning (ML) systems. This is subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: Quora's Privacy Policy explains how the company collects and processes personal data. You should review the Privacy Policy for more information.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you may give up the right to sue Quora in court.
* **Termination**: Either Quora or you can terminate the agreement, but the live document will describe the specific conditions.
* **Contact**: If you have questions about these Terms, please refer to Quora's published legal contact information.

As for clauses that may be potentially harmful to users:

* **Binding Arbitration**: As mentioned, this may limit your right to sue Quora in court. However, there is a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

Please note that these Terms seem to be focused on how Quora will use user data to improve its services, including AI and ML systems. If you're concerned about any specific provision, I recommend reviewing the Terms carefully and reading the Privacy Policy.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — QUORA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Quora and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Poe (Quora's AI chatbot platform): user prompts/responses may be used to improve Poe and partner models subject to settings, added bot-developer terms, and revised dispute resolution.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Quora to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.quora.com/about/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.quora.com/about/tos .

**Service Name:** 23andMe Terms of Service

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with 23andMe, a personal genomics company. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms apply to any product or service offered by 23andMe, as described on their official terms page.
* **User Content:** If you submit content to 23andMe, it may be used to improve and train their AI/ML systems, depending on your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** 23andMe's Privacy Policy explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. (The Privacy Policy is not reproduced in the Terms, but referenced instead.)
* **Dispute Resolution:** In case of a dispute, you and 23andMe will use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with some exceptions. This means you may not have the option to go to court if there's a problem.
	+ If you have a new account, you can opt-out of arbitration within 30 days.
	+ Additionally, some clauses limit your class-action rights, making it harder to join a group lawsuit.
* **Data Breaches:** In the event of a data breach, 23andMe requires users who don't explicitly opt out to use binding arbitration, which may limit their options.

**Clauses that may be Harmful to the User:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration:** This clause requires users to use binding arbitration for disputes related to data breaches within a 30-day opt-out window. Some users may not find arbitration suitable for resolving disputes.
* **Limited Class-Action Rights:** This clause limits your ability to join a group lawsuit, which may reduce your chances of resolving disputes collectively.

**Termination and Support:**

* Either party can terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
* For questions or concerns, 23andMe provides contact information and a link to their published Privacy Policy.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .
